title: Smoke from the reprocessing room
note: Fictional unit and patients. Your unit protocol, the attending nephrologist and your local disaster authorities decide every real event.
intro: You are a nurse in a ground-floor unit in Cebu City. You smell smoke and see it coming from under the reprocessing room door. Twelve patients are connected; three use wheelchairs and one came on a stretcher. The alarm has not sounded.

choices.text: Raise the alarm, close the door if safe, tell the charge nurse; someone free calls the fire bureau.
choices.feedback: Alarm and contain first; roles go to people who are free. A staff member without a patient calls the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP).

choices.text: Leave the patient you are with and run for the extinguisher, since a small fire is easiest to put out early.
choices.feedback: A staff member never leaves a connected patient alone to fetch an extinguisher.
choices.then: Your patient’s alarm sounds; another nurse covers. The charge nurse raises the alarm.

choices.text: Open the door to see how big the fire is before deciding whether to evacuate.
choices.feedback: Opening the door feeds the fire and lets smoke out.
choices.then: Smoke pours out; you close it and raise the alarm.

n2.scene: The technician tried an extinguisher on a small flame, but smoke keeps coming.

choices.text: He leaves and closes the door; the lead orders evacuation and oxygen off.
choices.feedback: Fight only a small fire with an exit behind you; when it grows, leave and contain. The incident lead asks for oxygen not in use to be turned off.

choices.text: He keeps fighting it with a second extinguisher, since the fire is still small and he is trained.
choices.feedback: A growing fire in a room with chemicals is for firefighters.
choices.then: The smoke thickens; the incident lead orders him out and the evacuation.

n3.prompt: How are patients taken off and moved?

choices.text: Staff take patients off one by one, nearest the smoke first; helpers move the rest by the sheet.
choices.feedback: In a fire there is rarely time to return blood. Mobility categories and helpers were set at the start of the shift. Clamp and disconnect, catheter clamps closed before separating lines, pressure on fistula sites; helpers move wheelchair and stretcher patients by the evacuation sheet.

choices.text: Return each patient’s blood fully before disconnecting, so nobody leaves with a blood loss.
choices.feedback: Rinse-back takes minutes per patient that a fire does not give.
choices.then: The incident lead orders clamp and disconnect for the rest.

choices.text: Tell patients to disconnect themselves to save time while staff move the wheelchairs.
choices.feedback: Patients are not taught to self-disconnect; under stress it causes bleeding and air entry.
choices.then: A patient bleeds from a pulled needle; a nurse presses it and takes over.

n4.scene: Across the street, the census nurse checks the list. One patient, Mrs. Dela Paz, is not checked off.

choices.text: Report at once to the incident lead for the firefighters; nobody re-enters.
choices.feedback: Firefighters search; staff stay out. The incident lead tells the firefighters where she was last seen.

choices.text: Two nurses go back in to look for her quickly, since they know the unit layout.
choices.feedback: Re-entering a burning building risks more lives.
choices.then: The incident lead stops them at the door and tells the firefighters.

choices.text: Assume she went home with her family, and call her phone once everyone is settled.
choices.then: A firefighter asks for the count; you report her missing.

end.title: Counted
end.text: Mrs. Dela Paz had left with her daughter and is recorded as leaving. Everyone is accounted for. The unit stays closed until the building is cleared.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Never leave a connected patient to fetch an extinguisher; give that job to someone free.
  • In a fire, clamp and disconnect is usually right; patients never disconnect themselves.
  • A named census nurse counts every patient; nobody re-enters a burning building.
